title: Fujitsu launches an AI service for modernising legacy systems
description: Fujitsu launched an AI-driven Modernization Service on 14 July 2026 that uses generative AI to help companies update legacy systems.
body:
On July 14, 2026, Fujitsu Limited announced the Japan launch of its highly anticipated Fujitsu AI-driven Modernization Service, a significant leap forward in enterprise digital and AI transformation. This new service promises to revolutionize how businesses handle their complex legacy systems by integrating cutting-edge generative AI with Fujitsu's decades of system integration expertise. The initiative is set to support the sustainable growth of businesses and organizations, particularly those grappling with the urgent need to modernize their foundational IT infrastructure to remain competitive in a rapidly evolving digital landscape.

The Dawn of AI-Powered Legacy System Transformation

The imperative for modernization has never been more critical, especially with the accelerated pace of digital transformation (DX) and AI transformation (AX) across industries. Sectors like finance, public services, and healthcare, which frequently face regulatory revisions, alongside manufacturing and distribution, with their complex operational management built on years of legacy systems, are under immense pressure to adapt. Fujitsu's new service directly addresses these challenges by automating and optimizing modernization initiatives, primarily focusing on rewrite and rehost approaches.

This service combines Fujitsu's proprietary AI platform, Fujitsu Kozuchi, and its Takane large language model (LLM), with advanced AI technologies from industry leaders like Anthropic PBC's Claude and OpenAI's GPT. The synergy of these AI models, coupled with the practical knowledge of Fujitsu's specialized engineers, known as "Modernization Meisters," enables a speedy and high-quality transformation. This integrated approach can potentially shorten migration periods by approximately 40%.

How the Fujitsu AI-driven Modernization Service Works

At its core, the service leverages AI-driven automation to accelerate modernization. It comprehensively analyzes various data from target legacy assets, centralizing them as AI-ready structured data through Fujitsu's proprietary AI technology. This process streamlines the identification of core information for modernization.

  • AI-Driven Automation: The service uses AI to analyze legacy system data and manage it as structured data, crucial for modernization.
  • Multi-AI Modernization: By optimally utilizing multiple AI models, including Fujitsu Kozuchi, Takane LLM, Anthropic's Claude, and OpenAI's GPT, the service promotes customer DX.
  • Dedicated AI Agents: Specialized AI agents, trained on Fujitsu's extensive project data and knowledge base, ensure high-speed and high-precision modernization.
  • Self-Service Platforms: Fujitsu plans to sequentially provide self-service AI platforms, empowering customers to perform modernization tasks themselves, leveraging the practical insights gained from this service.

The service is designed to free customers from the burden of optimally selecting and operating rapidly evolving AI technologies, allowing them to focus on core initiatives like business transformation and maximizing ROI.

Why This Matters for Productivity and Online Tools

The launch of Fujitsu's AI-driven Modernization Service signifies a critical shift in how enterprises will enhance their productivity and leverage online tools. As of 2026, AI agents are evolving beyond simple chatbots into autonomous, goal-oriented systems that can reason, plan, and execute complex, multi-step tasks without constant human supervision. These "digital employees" are reshaping workflows, decision-making, and operational efficiency across various industries.

For webonlinetools.com users, this means a future where backend complexities are drastically reduced, allowing for greater focus on front-end innovation and user experience. AI tools are already becoming indispensable partners in web development, handling repetitive tasks, optimizing performance, and accelerating design processes. Fujitsu's approach, which emphasizes automating the transformation of legacy systems, will accelerate the adoption of these advanced AI capabilities, making it easier for businesses to integrate next-gen AI into their digital infrastructure. This paves the way for faster website launches, smarter user experiences, and more personalized digital journeys.

"The speed, scale, and sophistication with which AI can perform tasks is compressing timelines, forcing defenders to respond faster than ever before. Vulnerability discovery that once required weeks or months of manual research can now happen in minutes."

This sentiment, expressed in discussions about AI security in 2026, underscores the necessity for AI-driven automation not just in development, but across the entire digital ecosystem, including security and performance optimization, areas where AI plays a critical role in safeguarding digital assets and ensuring fast user experiences.

The Broader Impact and Future Implications of AI Agents

The move towards more autonomous AI agents, as demonstrated by Fujitsu's new service and other industry trends, is a major theme in July 2026. Experts indicate that the industry is shifting from chasing raw model size to optimizing for usefulness, cost, and reliability. The ability of AI to independently complete multi-step tasks, while requiring narrow scope and human guardrails, is proving transformative.

This trend is also evident in developments like Sber's GigaChat 3.5 Ultra, launched yesterday, which expands support for autonomous AI agents capable of independently completing multi-step tasks and processing lengthy documents with improved speed and accuracy. Such advancements mean that AI agents can orchestrate complex workflows across multiple enterprise systems, monitoring incoming leads, analyzing customer data, and even generating personalized proposals, thereby automating end-to-end processes rather than isolated tasks.

What's Next for AI-Driven Modernization

The launch of the Fujitsu AI-driven Modernization Service is a clear indicator of the direction AI is heading – towards deeper integration, enhanced autonomy, and a focus on solving complex, real-world business challenges. As Fujitsu plans to roll out self-service platforms, the accessibility of these sophisticated AI tools will empower an even broader range of organizations to take control of their modernization journeys. We can expect to see continued investment in multi-AI strategies, combining specialized models for optimal performance, and further advancements in AI agents that can learn, adapt, and operate with increasing independence. This will not only lead to significant productivity gains for businesses but also reshape the very nature of work, with humans focusing more on strategic problem-solving and creative endeavors, while AI handles the intricate and often tedious tasks of digital transformation.
